headline: You can create a Slack app and open it to any workspace the same day with no review, but unlisted commercial apps read message history at 1 call a minute (15 messages) and Slack's terms reserve commercial distribution for the Marketplace, which needs 10 active workspaces and then up to about 12 weeks of review.

notes: Slack apps install with OAuth v2: slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize, then oauth.v2.access. Bot scopes go in scope=, user scopes in user_scope=.
Redirect URLs must be HTTPS and are saved under OAuth & Permissions; the redirect_uri must match or be a subdirectory of one of them.
No dynamic client registration: Slack's only discovery document is for Sign in with Slack and has no registration_endpoint.
PKCE is generally available since 30 March 2026 (turning it on is one-way); optional scopes since 16 March 2026.
Apps can be created from a YAML/JSON manifest in the dashboard, by a pre-filled link, or with apps.manifest.create (needs an app configuration token).

paths.label: Your own workspace only (internal app)
paths.summary: Create the app in your own Slack workspace (or Enterprise org) and never turn on public distribution. Anyone in that workspace can connect through Composio's OAuth flow. No review, full Tier 3 rate limits on message history, and the Real-time Search API and Slack MCP server are allowed for internal apps.

badges.text: If your workspace has 'Require approved apps' turned on, a workspace owner must approve or install the app first.

start_here.action: Create the app from the drafted manifest in your company workspace (api.slack.com/apps → Create New App → From a manifest).
Copy the Client ID, Client Secret and Verification Token from Basic Information → App Credentials, then connect a test account.

paths.label: Public distribution, unlisted
paths.summary: Click Activate Public Distribution and any Slack workspace can install the app through OAuth, with no review. It is meant for pilots: since 29 May 2025, new installs of commercially distributed non-Marketplace apps can call conversations.history and conversations.replies only once a minute (15 messages per call), the Real-time Search API and Slack MCP server are off-limits, and Slack's API Terms require a Marketplace or partner agreement to distribute commercially.

badges.text: conversations.history and conversations.replies: 1 request per minute, at most 15 messages per call, for new apps and new installs since 29 May 2025 (internal and Marketplace apps keep Tier 3, 50+ per minute).
Unlisted apps cannot use the Real-time Search API (assistant.search.context) or the Slack MCP server.

Selling a product that connects to Slack counts as commercial distribution, even when you hand customers a custom app or template; the API Terms require the Marketplace agreement or a Slack/Salesforce partner agreement for that.
Apps used outside your organisation must have a user agreement and privacy policy where users install them.
Customer workspaces can require owner approval for apps or allow only Marketplace apps; members then see a warning or must submit a request.

start_here.action: Create the app from the drafted manifest, then Manage Distribution → Activate Public Distribution.
Design around the 1-per-minute history limit: capture messages with event triggers instead of paging history.
If you charge for your product (or it connects to a paid one), plan the Marketplace listing now: unlisted is for pilots.

paths.label: Slack Marketplace listing
paths.summary: The route Slack intends for commercial apps. You first need the app installed and in use on 10+ active workspaces (sandboxes do not count), then a preliminary review (up to 10 business days) and a functional review (up to 10 weeks). Listed apps keep normal rate limits and can use the Real-time Search API, but search:read is not accepted and history, search and files scopes get an enhanced review.

gates.title: Marketplace preliminary review
gates.trigger: Submitting from 'Submit to the Slack Marketplace' in app settings, once the app has 10+ active workspace installs. Slack checks listing information, links, scope reasons and that it can install the app.

wait.note: Slack states 'up to'. Each resubmission at this stage resets your place in the queue. Your submission page shows the current estimate.

gates.title: Marketplace functional review
gates.trigger: A reviewer installs and tests the app and every scope; history, search and files scopes and user-token groups:write / mpim:write get an enhanced review.

wait.note: Slack states 'up to 10 weeks' for new submissions (6 weeks for changes to published apps) and will not expedite for launches.

badges.text: Public privacy policy, a landing page made for the Slack app (not behind a login) and a support page with replies within 2 business days.
Once listed, the app's configuration is locked: new scopes or features need re-review (up to 6 weeks).
Workspaces with 'Require approved apps' still need an owner to approve your listed app.

start_here.action: Create the app from the drafted manifest (without search:read), activate public distribution and start a pilot to reach 10 active workspaces.
Publish the privacy policy, landing page and support page; record the install-to-uninstall demo video.
Submit from 'Submit to the Slack Marketplace' with a reason for every scope; plan for up to 10 business days plus up to 10 weeks.

prerequisites.item: A Slack workspace where you can create apps (your company's, or a free Developer Program sandbox for testing).
prerequisites.why: Every Slack app is created in, and owned by, one workspace.

prerequisites.item: Workspace owner rights, or an owner willing to approve the app.
prerequisites.why: Workspaces with app approval turned on block installs until an owner approves.

prerequisites.item: A public privacy policy and user agreement for your agent.
prerequisites.why: Slack's API Terms require them for any app used outside your organisation; the Marketplace checks the privacy policy.

prerequisites.item: A public landing page for the Slack app and a support page with a contact that needs no extra account.
prerequisites.why: Marketplace reviewers check both; support replies are expected within 2 business days.

prerequisites.item: 10 or more active workspaces (used in the last 28 days, not sandboxes) running your app.
prerequisites.why: Submissions below the threshold are blocked; the count must hold for the whole review.

prerequisites.item: A test account for your own product, with dummy data, that reviewers can use.
prerequisites.why: Slack reviewers install the app themselves and cannot log in to your Slack workspaces.

steps.title: Create the Slack app from a manifest
steps.detail: Go to api.slack.com/apps → Create New App → From a manifest, pick the workspace that will own the app, paste the manifest below, click Next, then Create. Rename 'Your Agent'. The manifest asks for Composio's default Slack scopes as user-token scopes, because Composio's Slack toolkit acts as the signed-in user. For a Marketplace submission, delete search:read (and any scope your agent does not use) before creating. Or open the one-click link, which pre-fills the same manifest.

steps.title: Check the Redirect URL
steps.detail: In OAuth & Permissions → Redirect URLs, make sure Composio's callback is listed and saved (the manifest adds it). It must exactly match the redirect URI set in your Composio auth config, and Slack only accepts HTTPS. If you leave the auth config's redirect field at the Slack toolkit default, register the legacy URL instead (or add both: Slack accepts several Redirect URLs).

paste.label: Legacy redirect URI (only if the auth config keeps the toolkit default)

steps.title: Match the scopes to what your auth config requests
steps.detail: In OAuth & Permissions → Scopes, every scope your Composio auth config requests must be on the app, under the right token type. Several defaults (search:read, dnd:write, channels:write, users.profile:write, search:read.im/.mpim/.private) exist only as User Token Scopes. Remove scopes your agent will not use: smaller lists install more easily and are required for the Marketplace.

paste.label: User token scopes for a Marketplace submission (search:read removed)

steps.title: Copy the app credentials
steps.detail: Basic Information → App Credentials: copy the Client ID and Client Secret. Also copy the Verification Token (Composio's auth config asks for it to enable Slack triggers) and the Signing Secret (Composio's webhook endpoint for your own app uses it). If you need DM, private-channel or reaction events, create an App-Level Token with authorizations:read under Basic Information → App-Level Tokens.

steps.title: Connect a test account and confirm scopes
steps.detail: Start a connection from Composio and look at the slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize URL it opens: scopes in user_scope= must be User Token Scopes on your app, scopes in scope= must be Bot Token Scopes. Approve, then check that the connected account works for one read tool and one write tool. If Slack shows an approval request, the workspace requires owner approval.

steps.title: Activate public distribution
steps.detail: Manage Distribution → Share Your App with Other Workspaces: complete every item in the checklist, then click Activate Public Distribution. From then on, any workspace can install through OAuth. Leave it off if only your own workspace will connect.

steps.title: Publish the privacy policy, user agreement, landing and support pages
steps.detail: Required by the API Terms for any app used outside your organisation. For the Marketplace, the privacy policy must say how third-party (Slack) data is handled and be linked from a landing page built for the Slack app; the support page needs a contact that does not require another account. If your agent uses an LLM, add a note on the landing page that answers may be inaccurate. Slack's Developer Policy bans training LLMs on Slack data for every app.

steps.title: Check the public pages load without a login
steps.detail: We can check that your privacy policy, landing page and support page are public URLs that load without signing in.

steps.title: Reach 10 active workspaces
steps.detail: Run a pilot with early customers on the unlisted app until at least 10 workspaces that are not sandboxes have used it in the last 28 days. The count must stay at 10 or more throughout the review. History calls are rate-limited for these pilot installs.

steps.title: Write a reason for every scope and the AI disclosures
steps.detail: Slack wants to know how your app uses each scope, not what the scope does. Only include scopes the reviewer can test. History, search and files scopes get an enhanced review; user-token *:history scopes need a clear use case. Use user-token scopes only where the agent must act as the user. If you use Slack's agent (assistant) interface, Slack expects zero-copy: keep IDs, fetch content when needed. Fill in the AI fields in the Security & Compliance section.

paste.label: Scope reasons (edit to match your agent)
paste.value:
chat:write: The agent posts its answer in the channel or DM where the user asked it, as that user. Shown in the demo video at <mm:ss>.
channels:history: When a user asks the agent about a public channel, the agent reads recent messages in that channel at that moment to answer. It only reads channels the user can already see, and we do not store message content (we keep IDs only). Shown at <mm:ss>.
im:history / mpim:history / groups:history: Same as channels:history for DMs and private channels the user is in, used only on the user's explicit request. Remove these if your agent does not need them.
users:read: Resolve user IDs in messages to names so answers are readable.
<scope>: <what the user does> → <what the agent does with this scope> → <where the demo shows it>.

paste.label: AI disclosures (Security & Compliance section)
paste.value:
Model used: <provider and model name>
Retention: Slack data is held for <N> days only to answer the user's request; it is never used to train models.
LLM data tenancy: <single-tenant / multi-tenant, provider zero-retention setting>
LLM data residency: <region>

steps.title: Record the demo video
steps.detail: Show the full installation and OAuth flow, set-up, end-to-end use of every scope, and uninstalling.

steps.title: Prepare reviewer test access
steps.detail: Create a test account for your product with dummy data and an install link reviewers can use themselves. Do not give them your Slack workspace logins: they cannot use them.

steps.title: Submit to the Slack Marketplace
steps.detail: Open 'Submit to the Slack Marketplace' in your app's settings, fix anything the automated checks flag, review the listing and scopes, add the test account details and video link, and submit. If your product lets users build automations across apps, Slack also requires limiting installs to paid Slack plans (team.billing:read). Feedback arrives in the submission flow and by email.

steps.title: Answer reviewer feedback
steps.detail: Address every point. Resubmitting during the preliminary stage resets your place in the queue, so fix everything at once. After approval you choose when to publish.

while_you_wait.text: Build and test in your own workspace or a free Developer Program sandbox: internal apps keep normal rate limits and can use the Real-time Search API.
Run your pilot on the unlisted app to reach 10 active workspaces; sandboxes do not count towards the Marketplace minimum.
Read messages through event triggers rather than history calls, so pilot installs are not stuck on the 1-per-minute limit.
While installs accumulate, write the privacy policy, landing and support pages, scope reasons, AI disclosures and demo video.

blockers.symptom: The agent gets at most 15 messages per call and 'ratelimited' (HTTP 429) errors after one conversations.history or conversations.replies call per minute.
blockers.cause: Since 29 May 2025, new installs of commercially distributed apps that are not in the Slack Marketplace get these two methods at 1 request per minute and 15 objects per call.
blockers.fix_now: Capture messages as they arrive with event triggers instead of paging history, cache what you read, and honour Retry-After. For your own company, use an app that stays in your workspace: internal apps keep Tier 3 limits.
blockers.fix_properly: Get the app listed in the Slack Marketplace; listed apps keep Tier 3 limits.

escalate.how: Open a Developer Support request from a Slack account that collaborates on the app; include the app ID.
escalate.draft: Hi Slack Developer Support, our app <App ID> is receiving the non-Marketplace limits on conversations.history (1 request per minute, 15 messages). It is <internal to our workspace / in Marketplace review since <date>>. Can you confirm how the app is classified and whether the limits should apply? Thanks.

blockers.symptom: Users see 'This app isn't listed in the Slack Marketplace' or are asked to submit a request instead of an Allow button.
blockers.cause: The customer's workspace owner turned on 'Require approved apps' or allows only Marketplace apps.
blockers.fix_now: Ask a workspace owner to approve the app, install it themselves, or relax the setting in Settings → Apps & Workflows → App Management Settings.
blockers.fix_properly: List the app in the Slack Marketplace so Marketplace-only workspaces can install it; owners who require approval still have to approve it once.

escalate.how: Send the customer's Slack workspace owner a short approval request.
escalate.draft: Hi, to connect <Product> to Slack we need the app '<App name>' approved in our workspace. It requests these permissions: <scope list>, used to <purpose>. Please approve it in Slack under Apps → App Management Settings → app requests, or tell me if you have questions.

blockers.symptom: Slack shows a 'bad_redirect_uri' or redirect URI mismatch error when a user tries to connect.
blockers.cause: The redirect_uri Composio sends is not an HTTPS Redirect URL saved on the Slack app (for example the v3 callback is registered but the auth config still uses the legacy v1 URL).
blockers.fix_now: Add the exact URL from your Composio auth config under OAuth & Permissions → Redirect URLs and click Save URLs.
blockers.fix_properly: Keep the auth config's redirect URI and the Slack app's Redirect URLs in sync whenever either changes, and use one Slack app per Composio project.

escalate.how: If the URLs match exactly and the error persists, open a Developer Support request with the app ID and the full authorize URL.
escalate.draft: Hi, our app <App ID> returns bad_redirect_uri although https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback is saved under Redirect URLs. Authorize URL used: <url>. Could you check what Slack expects?

blockers.symptom: Connecting fails with an invalid scope error, or tools fail with 'missing_scope' / 'Insufficient scopes'.
blockers.cause: A scope the auth config requests is not on the Slack app, sits under the wrong token type (several defaults are user-token only), or the user declined an optional scope.
blockers.fix_now: Add the missing scope under the token type the authorize URL uses (user_scope= vs scope=), save, and reconnect the account.
blockers.fix_properly: Request only the scopes your tools need and keep the Slack app and the auth config scope lists identical.

escalate.how: Open a Developer Support request with the app ID, the scope and the exact error.
escalate.draft: Hi, our app <App ID> requests the user scope <scope>, which is configured under User Token Scopes, but installation fails with <error>. Could you tell us what is missing?

blockers.symptom: You cannot submit to the Marketplace, or the submission comes back from the preliminary review.
blockers.cause: Fewer than 10 active non-sandbox workspaces; a scope Slack does not accept (search:read, admin.*) or a broad history/files scope without a clear use case; or an app with little functionality inside Slack.
blockers.fix_now: Remove search:read, give a how-we-use-it reason for every remaining scope, and keep the pilot at 10+ active workspaces.
blockers.fix_properly: Give the agent real in-Slack features (answers in threads, App Home, shortcuts) and move message reading to the Real-time Search API once listed.

escalate.how: Email feedback@slack.com with questions about the review; answer reviewer feedback in the submission flow.
escalate.draft: Hi Slack Marketplace team, our app <App ID> (<name>) is an AI agent that <one-line purpose>. Before we resubmit, could you confirm whether <scope> is acceptable for <use case>, or which alternative you recommend? Thanks.

checks.detail: Anyone signed in to a Slack workspace can create an app at api.slack.com/apps, including from a pasted manifest.
Activate Public Distribution lets any workspace install with no review, but Slack positions this for pilots and rate-limits history calls for new installs.

No scope tiers for internal or unlisted apps. For the Marketplace, search:read is not accepted and search:read.*, *:history, files:read and user-token groups:write / mpim:write get an enhanced review.
Only for a Marketplace listing: a preliminary review and a functional review.
No third-party assessment or fee. Slack may run its own security review (scans, manual testing) on published Marketplace apps, at a time it chooses.
No install or user cap is documented for unlisted apps; the constraint is the history rate limit. The Marketplace instead needs a minimum of 10 active workspaces.

A user agreement and privacy policy for any app used outside your organisation; the Marketplace also wants a public landing page and support page. No legal-entity or domain verification is documented.
No fees: Slack does not charge for Marketplace inclusion. But commercial distribution needs the Marketplace agreement or a Slack/Salesforce partner agreement.
There is no test mode. Apps in their own workspace are fully featured; developer sandboxes are free; unlisted installs get the 1-per-minute history limit and no Real-time Search or MCP.
Preliminary review up to 10 business days; functional review up to 10 weeks (6 weeks for changes to listed apps). No expediting.
Developer Support request form, feedback@slack.com for Marketplace and review questions, and feedback inside the submission flow.

unknowns.question: How does Slack decide that an unlisted app is 'commercially distributed' for the history rate limit?
unknowns.why: A free pilot with a few customer workspaces may or may not get the 1-per-minute limit; this decides whether an unlisted pilot can read history usefully.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Install the unlisted app on a second workspace and call conversations.history twice within a minute; or ask Developer Support.

unknowns.question: Will Slack accept an AI agent whose main interface is outside Slack?
unknowns.why: The guidelines reject apps that do not include functionality in Slack, act as third-party Slack clients, or only provide an MCP server. If rejected, the only commercial route left is a partner agreement.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Email feedback@slack.com describing the agent before investing in the pilot; add in-Slack features (thread replies, App Home).

unknowns.question: Does Composio send the default Slack scopes as user scopes or bot scopes?
unknowns.why: Composio's KB says the auth config 'scopes' field means bot scopes and user permissions go in 'user_scopes', while the defaults include user-only scopes such as search:read. The answer decides where the scopes go on the Slack app.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Start a connection and read the slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize URL: scope= lists bot scopes, user_scope= lists user scopes.

unknowns.question: Does the automation-platform rule (install only on paid Slack plans, team.billing:read) apply to your agent?
unknowns.why: If Slack treats your agent as an automation platform, you must block free-plan workspaces, which shrinks your pilot pool.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Ask feedback@slack.com, or plan for team.billing:read in the submission.

unknowns.question: Does Slack's own advanced security review run on every new listing, and how long does it add?
unknowns.why: Slack only says it 'may be performed' and will not say when; it is a first-party review, so it does not change the level, but it could add time.
unknowns.how_to_find_out: Watch for mail from slack-marketplace-security@salesforce.com after approval; ask in the submission flow.

composio_notes.text: Composio's managed Slack app is not in the Slack Marketplace yet (Composio says its review is in progress). Users of Marketplace-only or approval-required workspaces will be blocked or asked for approval, and as a non-Marketplace app it is likely subject to the 1-per-minute history limit for new installs (our inference).

The Slack toolkit acts as the signed-in user. Composio's KB says the auth config 'scopes' field is bot scopes and user-token permissions go in 'user_scopes'; mirror whatever the authorize URL requests on the Slack app.

The auth config has an optional verification_token field, described as required to enable Slack triggers (Basic Information → App Credentials). Slack calls verification tokens deprecated; Composio's webhook endpoint for your own app uses the Signing Secret plus an optional authorizations:read app-level token. Have all three ready.
Webhook ingress is per Composio project: one Slack app can feed triggers to only one Composio project, so use separate Slack apps for staging and production projects.

The optional generic_id connection field passes a workspace ID to Slack. Composio says Slack will then only allow that workspace, but Slack treats the team parameter as a hint and can fall back to another workspace: check the connected workspace after each connection.
